text: [FAKE FIXTURE TEXT - NOT A REAL FILING - FAKEA FY2023] Item 1A. Risk Factors. FAKEA Corp (fictional) is a regional bank. Changes in market conditions, including rising interest rates, could reduce our net revenue and affect liquidity. We face significant exposure to commercial real estate loans, and a concentration in commercial real estate loans could increase credit or operating losses in fiscal 2023. Regulatory changes may raise our compliance costs and limit how we price our products.

[FAKE FIXTURE TEXT - NOT A REAL FILING - FAKEA FY2023] Item 1A. Risk Factors (continued). FAKEA Corp (fictional) depends on third-party vendors for critical systems. A failure or cybersecurity breach at a vendor could disrupt operations. We also face the risk of deposit outflows, which increased in fiscal 2023 as a result of inflation. Competition from larger firms could pressure margins, and we may be unable to retain key personnel.

[FAKE FIXTURE TEXT - NOT A REAL FILING - FAKEA FY2023] Item 1C. Cybersecurity. FAKEA Corp (fictional) maintains a cybersecurity risk management program overseen by the Chief Information Security Officer, who reports to the Audit Committee. During fiscal 2023 we detected a ransomware attempt at a third-party vendor; we do not believe it had a material effect on our business. In fiscal 2023 we adopted a new incident response plan. We perform annual penetration testing and assess third-party vendors before granting system access.

[FAKE FIXTURE TEXT - NOT A REAL FILING - FAKEA FY2023] Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis. For fiscal 2023, FAKEA Corp (fictional) reported that net revenue changed primarily due to rising interest rates and trends in commercial real estate loans. Operating expenses rose because of technology investment and higher compliance costs. Management monitors liquidity daily and maintains a revolving credit facility.

[FAKE FIXTURE TEXT - NOT A REAL FILING - FAKEA FY2023] Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis (continued). Liquidity and capital resources: FAKEA Corp (fictional) believes cash on hand and operating cash flows will be sufficient for at least the next twelve months.
